newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to urge banks to lend to borrowers abroad.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to urge banks to lend to borrowers abroad.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday measures would be introduced to encourage Thai-based offshore banking units to lend more funds to borrowers in third countries.

Rerngchai told reporters Thai banks would likely be asked to raise the ratio of their out-in loans based on their dollar and baht debt exposure, while foreign banks would be encouraged to balance their out-in and out-out loans. He did not elaborate.
Out-in loans are foreign borrowings brought in for relending to Thai-based clients. Out-out loans refer to offshore funds lent to borrowers in third countries but processed by Thai-based banks.

The planned measures, pending approval by the finance minister, were aimed at increasing out-out loans extended by offshore banking units while trimming their current out-in loans to domestic clients.

The governor said Thai banks have handled a disproportionately high amount of out-in loans which, central bank officials said earlier, had led to a rapid rise in Thailand's short-term private debts this year.
The governor said the Thai Bankers Association had displayed its support for the pending measures.
